column1: # THE TARGET MEMBERSHIP TABLE: the one source of membership the screening tool
# THIS FILE CAN BE EDITED BY HAND. If a target's member and competitor bins are
# wrong, every separation ratio comes out wrong. For every target the tool also
# measures the pair ALREADY in the panel with the same engine and compares it
# against the panel's published value; on a large divergence it prints a WARNING
# on the screen, and this file is the first place to look when it does.
#   hedef      the target name exactly as it stands in the panel
#   uye_taxid  a comma separated taxid list. "*A1", "*A2", "*B", "*F1" and "*F2"
#              mean every bin in that amplicon class. "KUTU:F2-1_500148" means
#              ONE SINGLE BIN, and once KUTU: appears on a row the membership is
#              read bin by bin AND NO LONGER BY TAXID.
#              WHY: a taxid is not enough to express membership. F2-1_500148,
#              F2-2_500148 and F2-4_500148 carry the same Kraken taxid while
#              their measured identities are Petriella setifera, Petriella
#              setifera, and "an unnameable lineage whose nearest record is
#              Lomentospora". Membership written by taxid counts all three as
#              members, but the third is a COMPETITOR and it is exactly the one
#              that drops the Petriella genus pair, at 1655 of 3000 reads.
#              The rule: MEMBERSHIP GOES BY THE MEASURED IDENTITY, NOT by the
#   haric      counted as neither a member nor a competitor: a close relative
#              deliberately left outside. The "KUTU:" prefix can be used here too.
#   kaynak     PANEL means it is written explicitly in targets.tsv.
#              TURETILDI means it was derived from the target name and

The measurement says the opposite: F1-1_44689 is Zoopagomycota_gen_Incertae_sedis sp. at genus level and 100 per cent, F1-2_44689 and F1-3_44689 are an unnameable lineage whose nearest record EU825622 is Opisthokonta > Nucletmycea at 96.70 per cent, and F1-4_44689 is an unnameable lineage whose nearest record JX974768 sits in the same clade at 67.08 per cent. All four are on the fungal side and not one is Amoebozoa; three of them are amplified by the universal pair as well (1775 of 2118, 879 of 1086, 2460 of 3000). So excluding them was wrong and the single protocol counting them as members was right.
